types.description: Same trigger leads to multiple identical actions, resulting in resource waste.
types.example: IF hallway_motion_sensor.motion_sensor_value == true THEN hallway_light.light_status = on; IF hallway_motion_sensor.motion_sensor_value == true THEN hallway_light.light_status = on

types.description: Same or similar trigger leads to mutually exclusive actions on the same device, causing system instability.
types.example: IF living_room_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value > 25 THEN living_room_AC.AC_mode = cool; IF living_room_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value > 25 THEN living_room_heater.heater_status = on

types.description: Rules trigger each other in an infinite cycle, causing the system to oscillate endlessly.
types.example: IF living_room_light.light_status == on THEN living_room_window.window_status = open; IF living_room_window.window_status == open THEN living_room_light.light_status = on

types.description: One rule's effect is always immediately overridden by another rule with a broader or encompassing trigger condition, rendering the first rule permanently ineffective.
types.example: IF living_room_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value > 28 THEN living_room_fan.fan_status = on; IF living_room_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value > 20 THEN living_room_fan.fan_status = off

types.description: A rule whose preconditions can never be simultaneously satisfied under the given device configuration, making it permanently inactive.
types.example: Rule 1: IF kitchen_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value > 30 THEN kitchen_AC.AC_status = on; Rule 2: IF kitchen_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value < 20 THEN kitchen_AC.AC_status = on (both rules target the same device under mutually exclusive conditions, one will never fire in the other's context)

types.description: Continuous action without a termination or feedback condition, potentially causing device overuse or dangerous physical states.
Action contradicts physical reality or safety logic, producing a response that worsens the detected situation.
Parameters set beyond physical possibility or sensor range, indicating a misunderstanding of device capabilities.
Related rules use inconsistent or overlapping thresholds for the same parameter, causing device state oscillation.
types.example: IF bedroom_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value > 25 THEN bedroom_AC.AC_status = on; IF bedroom_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value > 23 THEN bedroom_AC.AC_status = off

types.description: A safety-critical action is triggered without sufficient preconditions or contextual guards to ensure safe execution.
types.example: IF kitchen_smoke_sensor.smoke_sensor_value == true THEN kitchen_window.window_status = open

types.description: A rule's action produces unintended physical environment side effects that are not accounted for in the rule logic.
types.example: IF bathroom_humidifier.humidifier_status == on THEN bathroom_window.window_status = open

types.description: Externally manipulable environmental inputs trigger sensitive security actions, enabling adversary exploitation.
Unrelated or low-priority events trigger high-privilege operations, violating the principle of least privilege.
types.example: IF kitchen_smoke_sensor.smoke_sensor_value == true THEN front_porch_smart_lock.smart_lock_status = unlocked

types.description: Multiple individually benign rules combine to form a chain that achieves unauthorized access or privilege escalation.
types.example: Rule 1: IF living_room_curtain.curtain_status == closed THEN living_room_camera.secure_mode = off; Rule 2: IF living_room_camera.secure_mode == off THEN front_porch_smart_lock.smart_lock_status = unlocked

types.description: Indirect rule chains circumvent safety protection mechanisms through intermediate device state changes.
types.example: Rule 1: IF bedroom_temperature_sensor.temperature_sensor_value > 35 THEN bedroom_window.window_status = open; Rule 2: IF bedroom_window.window_status == open THEN bedroom_smart_lock.smart_lock_status = unlocked

types.description: A single device failure or erroneous sensor reading propagates through the rule chain, affecting multiple downstream devices.
types.example: Rule 1: IF kitchen_smoke_sensor.smoke_sensor_value == true (false alarm) THEN kitchen_gas_sensor.gas_sensor_valve = closed; Rule 2: IF kitchen_gas_sensor.gas_sensor_valve == closed THEN kitchen_oven.oven_status = off; Rule 3: IF kitchen_oven.oven_status == off THEN kitchen_speaker.speaker_status = on

types.description: A normal operation in one room triggers a rule chain that degrades the security level of another room.
types.example: Rule 1: IF kitchen_smoke_sensor.smoke_sensor_value == true THEN kitchen_window.window_status = open; Rule 2: IF kitchen_window.window_status == open THEN garage_garage_door.garage_door_status = open
